topic: The Netherlands below the sea: a 15-second sample
method: Well-documented figures; links not re-opened from this container (blocked here). Terrain from Mapzen elevation tiles (SRTM-based, about 30-90 m cells, a few metres of vertical error): the flooded areas are approximate, not the official AHN map. Check before publishing.

claims.claim: In the North Sea flood of 31 January to 1 February 1953, 1,836 people died in the Netherlands.
claims.notes: More died in England, Belgium and at sea; the figure here is the Netherlands only.

claims.claim: About a quarter (26%) of the Netherlands lies below sea level.

sources.title: PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency (2010): 26% below sea level, 29% prone to river flooding
sources.quote: [summary] 26% of the country lies below sea level

sources.title: Government of the Netherlands: water management
sources.quote: [summary] about a quarter below sea level

contradictions: Popular sources sometimes say 'a third'; PBL's 26% is the official figure.
claims.notes: Map frame: centred at 52.2N 5.3E, 260 km across (shown on screen). The water starts at -7 m, just below the lowest point, Zuidplaspolder (-6.76 m NAP); the gauge reads the level as it rises.

claims.claim: In 1953 the sea reached 4.55 m above NAP (Dutch mean sea level) at Vlissingen, the highest level recorded there.
claims.notes: The peak varied along the coast; the film applies the Vlissingen figure evenly and says so (illustrative).

claims.claim: On the night of 31 January to 1 February 1953, a severe storm drove a surge south down the North Sea from north of Scotland onto the coasts of England, the Netherlands and Belgium.

sources.title: Met Office: the 1953 North Sea flood
sources.quote: [summary] the storm surge travelled down the North Sea

sources.title: North Sea flood of 1953 (Wikipedia)
sources.quote: [summary] storm north of Scotland, surge moved south

claims.notes: The arrow from north of Scotland (59.3N 0.5E) to Zeeland (51.6N 3.6E) shows the direction only (illustrative).
